summary: Iteration 20 pre-launch wiring audit (HRMS go-live). Backend smoke: 16/17 pytest cases pass for the 4 new feature surfaces (Comp-Off, Investment Declarations, Bulk Employee Import, Audit Log) plus login smoke for 4 roles. Frontend: all 4 new pages render with correct data-testids, 56-route sweep is clean except 1 uncaught AxiosError on /app/employee, RBAC gating verified for employee + manager + hr, header links (bell → /app/notifications, help → /app/help) work.

critical.issue: Returns 500 with 'TypeError: string indices must be integers, not str'. Bug in comp_off_routes.py line 136: call is `_ensure_balance(db, cid, row['employee_id'], lt['id'], year)` but the signature in leave_admin_routes.py line 147 is `_ensure_balance(db, company_id, emp_id, lt: dict, year)` — caller passes lt['id'] (a string) where a dict is expected, and the helper then tries lt['id'] on the string. Also the call treats the return value as a string (`bal_id = await ...`) then uses `bal_id` in `update_one({'id': bal_id})`, but the helper returns the balance DOCUMENT (dict). Two-part fix: (1) pass `lt` dict, (2) use `bal_id = (await _ensure_balance(...))['id']`. Approve flow is currently completely broken — this is a launch blocker for Comp-Off.

minor.issue: Response shape uses {row_count, new_rows, duplicate_rows, errors, warnings} — NOT the {valid_rows, errors, warnings} shape documented in the review request. Not a bug, but: (a) update the problem-statement docs, (b) the frontend BulkEmployeeImport.jsx must read the same keys. Also, the CSV template has 10 columns (email, name, employee_code, designation, department, branch_code, employee_type, phone, date_of_joining, manager_email), not 11 as stated in the review request — `ctc_annual` is documented in the backend OPTIONAL list + help text but is NOT in the downloadable template CSV header. Recommend adding `ctc_annual` to the template so users don't have to hand-edit.

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught AxiosError fires during mount (visible in page-error listener). Page still renders but an API call is rejecting without a catch handler, polluting the console and blocking any error-boundary work later. Does NOT crash the UI — just a hygiene issue. Reproduce: login as any role and visit /app/employee directly.

integration_issues.issue: GET /api/declarations/me?financial_year=<fy> returns 400 for FY values that have never existed in the DB — frontend swallows via catch and falls back to empty state, which is fine UX-wise but noisy in the console. Backend should arguably auto-create a draft (as the docstring claims) or return 200 with empty items rather than 400.

rca of the issue: Comp-off approve 500 root cause: in /app/backend/routers/comp_off_routes.py line 136, the call `await _ensure_balance(db, cid, row['employee_id'], lt['id'], year)` passes `lt['id']` (a string) as the 4th positional arg, but the helper in leave_admin_routes.py line 147 expects the full `lt` dict and does `lt['id']` internally → Python raises `TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str'` because you can't subscript a string with another string. Additionally, the return value is a dict but caller assigns it to `bal_id` and uses it in `update_one({'id': bal_id})` which would then mismatch even if arg was fixed. Mitigation: change to `bal = await _ensure_balance(db, cid, row['employee_id'], lt, year); bal_id = bal['id']`.
